newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Firmer despite high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Firmer despite high stocks.

text.p: Naphtha prices firmed on overnight crude strength, but gasoline was unchanged amid high stocks and weak demand, traders said.
Singapore weekly stocks of light distillates rose by 737,000 barrels to 6.795 million barrels in the week ending July 2.
Traders attributed the rise mainly to gasoline.
"Look at the storage levels, everyone has barrels," a trader said. "The market is still bearish.. there is still a lot of length in the region but not much requirement."
Gasoline traders were bearish in the outlook for August as Chinese and Korean supplies return to the market.
A Korean trader told Reuters there were "plentiful stocks and two refiners are looking to export to avoid high ullage".

The third refiner which is a regular exporter of gasoline, Yukong, is balanced as it plans to shut down its 50,000 barrel-per-day residue fluid catalytic cracker (RFCC) between August 2-September 10 for maintenance, an industry source said.
The Singapore fob market was dull with only a bid for 92-octane unleaded lifting July 29-August 2, bid at 22.25 per barrel.
Naphtha July swaps firmed by 20 cents per barrel to $20.80/$21.00, brokers said.
